AdventHealth Central Florida Division (Orlando). AdventHealth Cancer Institute diagnoses approximately 30,000 cancer cases annually, representing 20% of Florida’s estimated 145,000 annual cancer cases. In Central Florida, one in every two patients with cancer have cancer surgery at AdventHealth. The Cancer Institute has 17 cancer centers, with two more planned, 12 disease-site and subspecialty oncology programs, and more than 300 oncology providers. The program is ranked No. 1 for cancer care in the greater Orlando area by U.S. News & World Report. It offers over 250 oncology clinical trials, including 25 phase 1 studies, and 112 dedicated research employees, including principal investigators and research staff. AdventHealth is expanding quaternary cancer care with a new Central Florida cancer flagship, since an estimated one in five residents in the region require quaternary cancer care, which is the highest, most acute level of care. It is also home to the only Lymphatic Education & Research Network center of national excellence in the Southeast. AdventHealth leads the market in inpatient and outpatient cancer surgeries, and is Central Florida’s first and only blood and marrow transplant program. The program also reports some of the best outcomes in the nation for treating leukemia, lymphoma, myeloma and more. It is also one of the most active lung and esophageal clinical trial sites in the country. Its gynecological, brain and spine cancer programs are also among the top in the nation, with outcomes that exceed averages. Recent clinical milestones include performing a liver transplant for metastatic colon cancer and lymphatic bypass surgery.

Allina Health (Minneapolis). Allina Health Cancer Institute, a 128-bed program staffed by 188 specialists, launched the Twin Cities’ first histotripsy program in late 2025, using focused high-intensity sound waves to destroy liver tumors without surgery, and plans to pilot high-intensity focused ultrasound for prostate cancer in the third quarter of 2026. In 2025, the cancer institute introduced Pluvicto, a targeted theranostics therapy for prostate-specific membrane antigen-positive prostate cancer. Ann & Robert H. Lurie Children’s Hospital of Chicago. The Center for Cancer and Blood Disorders at Ann & Robert H. Lurie Children’s Hospital of Chicago treats more children with cancer and blood disorders than any other hospital in Illinois, caring for 220 new cancer patients each year. Lurie Children’s is ranked 19th in the nation for pediatric cancer care by U.S. News & World Report for 2025-26. Baptist Health South Florida (Coral Gables, Fla.). Baptist Health Cancer Care is anchored by the Herbert Wertheim Cancer Institute, the Christine E. Lynn Cancer Institute and multiple satellite locations. The program treats the second-most new cancer patients of any hospital system in Florida each year and consistently ranks in the top 10% of U.S. News & World Report‘s national cancer rankings. The gift helped establish the Herbert Wertheim Cancer Institute Transformational Impact Fund, a $100 million fund dedicated to advancing cancer care, research, prevention and education systemwide. Separately, Baptist Health reached a major construction milestone on a new proton therapy center at the Lynn Cancer Institute, bringing the precision therapy to patients in Palm Beach County, Fla. Sutter Health (Sacramento, Calif.). Sutter Health provides cancer care through an integrated network of 22 cancer centers across Northern California, each accredited by the Commission on Cancer, the American Society for Radiation Oncology and other national bodies. The system treats more than 129,000 cancer patients annually, cared for by more than 250 specialists delivering team-based treatment. The program diagnosed 22,000 new cancer cases in 2025. More than 80% of Sutter’s cancer patients are guided by National Comprehensive Cancer Network clinical pathways, and patients have access to more than 150 phase 1-4, industry and National Cancer Institute-sponsored clinical trials. Multidisciplinary tumor boards integrate research with care planning, and Sutter investigators publish findings in journals including JAMA Oncology, The Lancet and The New England Journal of Medicine. Clinical capabilities include CAR T-cell therapy, GammaTile neurosurgery, robotic-assisted procedures and targeted radiation therapies, supported by AI-enabled screening and detection tools that help catch cancer earlier. Sutter is also expanding its cancer footprint with a major expansion in Modesto, Calif., new ambulatory cancer services in Folsom and Santa Clara, Calif., and additional radiation oncology centers across the region.

In 2025, Fox Chase earned its strongest cancer center support grant score in more than two decades, published 692 scientific articles, enrolled patients in 207 clinical trials and drew more than $78 million across 435 active funded projects. The center also became the first hospital in Pennsylvania to achieve six Magnet recognition program renewals for nursing excellence, most recently in 2023, and its Blood Cancer and Cellular Therapy Institute recently surpassed 3,000 bone marrow transplants. ## Resting Rainbow of Orlando (Orlando, Florida)

An independently owned pet cremation and funeral home facility, Resting Rainbow of Orlando, recently opened in Florida. The facility, owned by Luis and Meylen Trujillo, offers services to walk-in and call-in customers, as well as to veterinary clinics and animal hospitals wanting to support their clients during a time of loss. Resting Rainbow also offers pet removal and delivery services, as well as memorial items like urns, jewelry, and other keepsakes. For law enforcement agencies in the community with K-9 officers who have passed away, Resting Rainbow is offering services free of charge.

"One of our primary goals was to establish a pet cremation process that is responsible, sustainable and transparent", said Luis Trujillo in a news release.^{2} "We were able to accomplish this goal by collaborating and partnering with Joseph Castranova, CEO of Resting Rainbow Franchise Corporation, who helped us source the proper equipment and to establish a transparent cremation process that is trackable from the moment of pet reception, to the moment pet remains are handed to our customers. Our equipment is a state-of-the-art multi-chamber pet cremation incinerator that is environmentally friendly and appealing. We welcome pet families to consider our private viewing and witness cremation services, an experience that will give them the opportunity to see the process being carried out for their beloved pet from an intimate setting inside our memorial room."

# Novartis to add radioligand therapy manufacturing facility in Winter Park, Florida, fourth in US to serve patients and advance $23 billion investment

Jan 09, 2026

  * New 35,000-square-foot facility in Winter Park will expand RLT manufacturing footprint to optimize delivery for patients across southeastern US
  * Purpose-built facility will strengthen Novartis RLT manufacturing network alongside existing Indiana, New Jersey, and recently completed California sites
  * Novartis RLT portfolio advancing with new isotopes, ligands and combination therapies, bringing innovation to new cancer types

Basel, January 9, 2026 – Novartis, a leading global innovative medicines company, today announced plans to build its fourth US radioligand therapy (RLT) manufacturing facility in Winter Park, Florida. The built-for-purpose, state-of-the-art facility represents another milestone in the company's $23 billion US investment announced in April 2025, further expanding manufacturing capabilities to meet growing demand for these cutting-edge cancer treatments. Novartis is scaling US manufacturing to bring innovative medicines closer to patients, so treatments are researched, made, and delivered with greater speed, reliability, and access in the communities where people live.
The new 35,000-square-foot facility in Winter Park, Florida, will come online by 2029 and will strengthen Novartis’ specialized supply chain and manufacturing capabilities across its network of RLT production facilities. The new facility will optimize the delivery of RLT medicines to patients in the southeast US and help maintain the company’s steady rate of >99% of doses administered on the planned day as the potential for this promising treatment modality continues to expand.
“Building this new facility in Florida marks an important step in fulfilling the promise of RLT for patients,” said Vas Narasimhan, CEO of Novartis. “Radioligand therapy has fundamentally changed how we approach certain cancers, and our growing US manufacturing network ensures we can continue to deliver these critical medicines with speed and reliability to patients who need them.”

# Sarasota Memorial Invests in Future Healthcare Access for One of Southwest Florida's Fastest-Growing Communities

Wednesday, September 23, 2026

SARASOTA, Fla. (Sept. 22, 2026) – With the four-county region expected to grow from approximately 1.2 million residents today to nearly 1.8 million over the next 25 years, Sarasota Memorial Health Care System (SMH) is moving forward with plans to acquire approximately 120 acres in Manatee County’s fast-growing State Road 64 corridor.

Located within Sarasota Memorial's four-county primary service area, the property just east of I-75 provides flexibility to meet both current and future healthcare needs and will help ensure the region’s only public, not-for-profit health system keeps pace with one of Southwest Florida's fastest-growing communities.

Approved by the Sarasota County Public Hospital Board on Tuesday, the nearly $60 million land deal is contingent upon SMH working with Manatee County officials and community leaders to rezone and develop a future campus on the site. In July, the Hospital Board also approved acquiring a 10-acre adjacent parcel with direct access to SR 64.Image: David Verinder

“This investment reflects the kind of long-range planning that has allowed Sarasota Memorial to serve our region for more than a century,” said David Verinder, CEO of Sarasota Memorial Health Care System. “Healthcare infrastructure takes years to plan and build. Securing strategically located property today allows us to improve our capacity to care for the community now, while enhancing access for future generations.”

Amid national shortage, veterinarians flock to Florida

New veterinary clinics are popping up in Florida amid an ongoing national vet shortage.
The big picture: The pandemic pet adoption boom aggravated the shortage, which has contributed to provider burnout.
By the numbers: The number of vet establishments across the country has gone up 8.4% since 2012, according to 2021 Census Bureau data, the most recent available.
Zoom out: Many more vets are probably still needed to meet demand.
Now two in three households own a pet, per American Pet Products Association data.
What we're watching: Veterinary schools are increasing class capacity and new vet schools are in development, Rosati said.
Of note: 64% of vets are women, per AVMA numbers.

## Future

Over the next few years, numerous expansion projects are planned for CCIRH. The Emergency Department is currently the site of a significant $5.5 million project. This project includes an 8,750 square foot expansion of the department, as well as the renovation of existing facilities. The project is currently under construction and is expected to finish in 2026. In addition, a $30-million third-floor expansion to the Scully-Welsh Cancer Center is currently being planned.
